sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Types / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: What does BMI stand for in physical health assessments?
questions.answer: B) Body Mass Index

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key component of health-related physical fitness?
questions.answer: C) Cardiovascular Endurance

questions.question_text: In track and field athletics, what is a 'baton' used for?
options: C) Passing to a teammate in a relay race
questions.answer: C) Passing to a teammate in a relay race

questions.question_text: True or False: Flexibility refers to the range of motion available at a joint.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question_text: Which fundamental athletic skill involves taking off from one foot and landing on the same foot?
questions.answer: B) Hopping

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a 'warm-up' before engaging in vigorous physical activity?
options: C) To prepare the body and prevent injuries
questions.answer: C) To prepare the body and prevent injuries

questions.question_text: Which of these is a field event in athletics?
questions.answer: B) Long Jump

questions.question_text: The ability to change the direction of the body quickly and accurately is known as:
questions.answer: C) Agility

questions.question_text: True or False: Physical education only benefits the physical development of a child and not their mental well-being.
questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: Which motor skill involves propelling an object away from the body using the hands?
questions.answer: B) Throwing

questions.question_text: State two benefits of maintaining good cardiovascular endurance. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Good cardiovascular endurance strengthens the heart, improves lung capacity, reduces fatigue during prolonged activities, and lowers the risk of lifestyle diseases.

questions.question_text: Differentiate briefly between a 'jump' and a 'leap' in athletic movements. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A jump involves taking off from one or both feet and landing on both feet, whereas a leap involves taking off from one foot and landing on the opposite foot.

questions.question_text: Why is 'reaction time' an important component of motor fitness? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Reaction time is crucial because it determines how quickly an individual can respond to a stimulus, like a starting gun in a race or an approaching ball.

questions.question_text: List two common measurements used to evaluate an individual's physical growth. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Two common measurements used to assess physical growth and development in students are standing height and body weight.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of performing a 'cool-down' routine after sports? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A cool-down gradually lowers the heart rate and breathing to normal levels, helps remove lactic acid from muscles, and reduces muscle stiffness.

questions.question_text: Explain the technique for a proper overhand throw in athletics, detailing the body positioning and release. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Stand sideways to the target, step forward with the opposite foot, rotate the hips and shoulders, bring the throwing arm forward from behind the ear, and release the ball with a wrist snap, following through across the body.

questions.question_text: Describe the basic phases of a long jump execution from start to finish. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The long jump consists of four phases: the approach run to build speed, the forceful takeoff from the board, the flight or hang in the air, and the two-footed landing in the sandpit.

questions.question_text: How does regular participation in physical education contribute to a student's mental and emotional well-being? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Physical education reduces stress and anxiety through exercise-induced endorphins. It builds self-confidence, improves concentration, and provides a healthy outlet for emotions, fostering overall mental resilience and a positive mood.

questions.question_text: Define 'Coordination' and provide one example of a sports activity that requires high hand-eye coordination. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Coordination is the ability to use different parts of the body together smoothly and efficiently. An example is hitting a pitched ball with a bat in cricket, which requires excellent hand-eye coordination.

questions.question_text: A student wants to improve their overall physical fitness to perform better in school athletic meets. Design a basic weekly training plan that incorporates cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, and flexibility. Explain why each component is necessary. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The plan should include jogging or swimming 3 days a week for cardiovascular endurance to sustain long activities. Include bodyweight exercises like push-ups and squats 2 days a week to build muscular strength for power. Finish every session with 10 minutes of stretching to improve flexibility, which prevents injuries and increases the range of motion.

questions.question_text: During a relay race, the baton exchange between two runners is consistently failing. Analyze the biomechanical and coordination factors involved in a successful 'non-visual' baton exchange, and suggest corrections for the runners. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: A successful non-visual exchange requires synchronized speed and precise timing. The outgoing runner must start accelerating at the right mark and extend their hand backward steadily. The incoming runner must call a verbal cue and place the baton firmly into the open hand. Corrections include practicing the timing mark, communicating clearly, and ensuring the receiving arm is stable.
